title: Calculus
summary: Isaac Newton invented calculus in the mid to late 1660s, while at home in Woolsthorpe when plague closed his university. He wrote a tract on fluxions in October 1666, unpublished but widely influential. About a decade later Gottfried Leibniz developed it independently, and more influentially. By 1675 Leibniz had settled on the notation still written today.

uncertainty.note: Spans the independent discoveries of infinitesimal calculus by Isaac Newton (1665–1666) and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1675), prior to early publication in 1684.
